about: Plot expressions as the server's extractors pass them to sample_function (** for ^, glyphs such as −, √ and | kept) and as a user types them into the phone's series editor, with the y SymPy gives at each x through the server's own reading (app.modules.math.solve._parse_expression, the parse sample_function plots). fence: the text sample_function writes into the graph fence's expr for it, SymPy's reading printed in the grammar the phone reads (app.modules.math.solve.graph_expr_text); the API test regenerates it and checks the server re-reads it to the same y. apps/mobile/lib/math/graphExpr.ts re-reads the fence text to resample on zoom, and the raw text in the series editor; both must agree within 1e-9 (relative above 1). A null y has no real, finite value there (outside the domain or at a pole): the phone must give NaN or an infinity, which its sampler drops. refused: neither side reads the text as a plot, so no fence is written. phone_gap: the server reads the raw text and the phone does not; the phone test skips its raw parity and checks the phone refuses rather than drawing a different curve, and still checks the fence text. Delete the line when the phone learns the raw form.

cases.note: Neither side reads a bracketless function before a power: SymPy's implicit application fails on it and the phone needs brackets. sin(x^2) and sin(x)^2 both read.

cases.phone_gap: The server reads a function name without brackets (SymPy implicit application: sin x is sin(x), cos 2x is cos(2x)); the phone parser needs the bracket and refuses this raw form. The graph fence never carries it: the server writes its reading (fence), which the phone reads and resamples.

The server reads a function name without brackets (SymPy implicit application: sin x is sin(x), cos 2x is cos(2x)); the phone parser needs the bracket and refuses this raw form. The graph fence never carries it: the server writes its reading (fence), which the phone reads and resamples.

The server rewrites √ before parsing (_rewrite_unicode_sqrts); the phone tokenizer has no √ and refuses this raw form. The graph fence carries sqrt(x) instead (fence), which the phone reads and resamples.

The server pairs bare bars into Abs (_rewrite_bare_abs_bars); the phone tokenizer has no | and refuses this raw form. The graph fence carries abs(x) instead (fence), which the phone reads and resamples.

The server splits the glued name xe into x times e (split_symbols); the phone reads xe as one unknown name and refuses this raw form. The graph fence carries x*e^x instead (fence), which the phone reads and resamples.
